CLAUDE.md

Source: CLAUDE.md

This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

Shared conventions

The portfolio’s shared rules are synced into .claude/shared/ from pedrobtz/packages:claude/shared/. Never edit them here. Where this file and a shared file disagree, this file wins for this package.

@.claude/shared/workflow.md @.claude/shared/r-package.md @.claude/shared/ci.md @.claude/shared/native-code.md @.claude/shared/correctness.md @.claude/shared/assurance.md

What this is

zucbor encodes R values as CBOR (RFC 8949) and decodes CBOR and CBOR sequences (RFC 8742) into ordinary R vectors and lists, through a vendored subset of TinyCBOR, so no system library is needed. Input is assumed untrusted (network peers, IoT devices, COSE, WebAuthn, CWT, CoAP): decoding checks the whole item against depth, size and item limits before building any R object. Encoding is deterministic: identical R objects give identical bytes on every platform. Zero hard runtime dependencies. It is the fourth self-describing format in a family with zujson, zuyaml and zuxml: when the design does not settle a question, look at how those packages do before inventing something new.

.agents/design.md is the specification and outranks this file: the R mapping in §6–§7, deterministic encoding §8, errors §10, limits §11, TinyCBOR vendoring and its build traps §13, decisions §18, open questions §19. A decision in §18 is settled unless the work shows it is wrong, and then the design changes in the same commit. .agents/roadmap.md records the stages to 0.1.0 (Stages 0–16, all done), each with a Status: line. Never put status in a stage heading, since that changes its anchor.

Current state

Verified 2026-11-11. 0.1.0 is on CRAN (published 2026-10-21; GitHub release 0.1.0 on commit f904184). main is 0.1.0.9000, with two fixes in NEWS.md so far. The full v1 API is built: the decoders, cbor_read*(), cbor_validate(), cbor_diagnose(), cbor_annotate(), the encoders, the value classes cbor_map(), cbor_tag(), cbor_simple(), cbor_bigint(), the as_cbor() generic and zucbor_info(). The roadmap’s Stage 9 and Stage 16 tables map each design §20 acceptance criterion to what verifies it.

Versions and dependents

The current version’s parent issue is #56 for v0.1.1. Its open sub-issues are #52 (zu-family conventions), #49 (zubin’s buffer and cursor) and #41 (zufast primitives). #57 is the reminder that the next submission opens from 2026-12-02. Sibling packages that depend on this one: none. No sibling is a confirmed consumer, so v1 is the R API only, with no C API and no archive.

Commands

Occasional, from the package root:

tools/verify-vendor              # vendor tree == pinned release
R CMD INSTALL -l <lib> . && tools/check-symbols <lib>/zucbor/libs/zucbor.so
tools/check-status-table         # status table == vendored cbor.h
tools/run-lint                   # project C warning-free under strict flags
tools/run-mutation-check         # every GUARD in the walk is load-bearing
tools/run-fuzz [seconds]         # libFuzzer over the R-free check phase
tools/run-conformance            # fixtures vs sources, cbor/test-vectors; network
tools/update-fixtures            # regenerate the conformance fixtures
tools/run-benchmarks             # against zujson (design §17)
tools/update-tinycbor <tag>      # re-vendor TinyCBOR

Run tools/check-symbols on an R CMD INSTALL build, not a load_all() one: load_all() compiles with -UNDEBUG, which leaves TinyCBOR’s assert()s in and makes the check fail, correctly. Re-run the benchmarks after changing the walk, the builder or the encoder. Apple’s clang has no libFuzzer, so run-fuzz needs a clang that ships it.

Architecture

Two phases (design §4), each in its own file:

  • Check (src/zu_walk.c), which is all of cbor_validate(): one iterative walk for limits, duplicate keys (by value, sorted per map), UTF-8, tag content and offsets. Four modes: one item, a sequence, a prefix, and a stream (cbor_read_seq(each =)), which stops before an item the input ends inside; truncation is CborErrorUnexpectedEOF and nothing else, which the fuzz target checks. cbor_value_validate() runs only for deterministic = TRUE. The walk returns a fault to R, which raises it with the user’s call through zu_raise_fault(). Status names map to condition classes in zu_status_class (R/conditions.R).
  • Build (src/zu_build.c) runs only after the check, takes container sizes from the check’s plan (never from length headers), and stages scalar array elements in C. It raises its own faults through zu_raise_fault() via R_FindNamespace, with the user’s call wrapped in quote(). zu_mkchar() there is the only place CBOR text becomes a CHARSXP.
  • Encoder (src/zu_encode.c, design §8) and diagnostic printer (src/zu_diag.c, §5) are project code; TinyCBOR contributes only its parser, validator and error strings.
  • src/init.c registers every .Call entry point (R_useDynamicSymbols(dll, FALSE), R_forceSymbols(dll, TRUE)), so R code calls .Call(zucbor_x), never .Call("zucbor_x").
  • fuzz/ holds the libFuzzer targets, canary, arena and probe; it is not in the tarball. The full file list is design §15.

Naming: R exports cbor_ (plus zucbor_info() and as_cbor()), R and C internals zu_, .Call entry points and condition classes zucbor_, and user-facing value classes cbor_, because users construct them.

Invariants that are easy to break

  • No R object before the whole item is checked. A nine-byte header can claim 2^64 elements; the build may only trust sizes the walk has backed with real bytes (design §4).
  • The check phase is R-free behind src/zu_check.h (zu_walk.c, zu_status.c, zu_float.c, zu_time.c): use zu_scratch(), zu_interrupt_check() and ZU_NO_OFFSET, never R_alloc() or R headers, or the fuzz build (-DZU_STANDALONE) breaks.
  • Security guards in the walk carry /* GUARD: name */ on their if line. tools/run-mutation-check proves each is load-bearing; add a case there for any new guard.
  • Do not switch on CborValidateTagUse: TinyCBOR’s table refuses valid tag 1 floats (design §3, §11).
  • Check an item’s type before any cbor_value_get_* call. Under R’s -DNDEBUG, TinyCBOR’s cbor_assert() becomes unreachable(), so a violated precondition is undefined behaviour, not an abort (§13, trap 3). The sanitizer jobs build with -UNDEBUG to make it visible.
  • Three decoder rules make cbor_encode(cbor_decode(b)) equal b, pinned by test-roundtrip.R and the COSE corpus: a one-element array decodes as an I() value, booleans do not join the numbers, and whole doubles encode as integers.
  • The encoder writes into a malloc() buffer owned by a finalized external pointer (and each non-text map key into one of its own). It is the only heap memory that crosses a longjmp.
  • User code runs mid-build and mid-encode (tag handlers via zu_run_handler(), as_cbor() methods). It may error, be interrupted or call zucbor again, so the build and the encoder keep no static state and hold everything PROTECTed or R_alloc()ed. Scratch allocated after a vmaxget() mark dies at its vmaxset(): never keep a pointer to it past that (the encoder’s map pools did, until Stage 10).
  • zu_raise_fault() builds its condition directly: do.call() would evaluate the user’s call again.
  • The design’s mapping tables, the roxygen docs and the tests are the same table three times. Change all three together.
  • NEWS.md keeps a versioned heading: R CMD check NOTEs a bare # zucbor (development version) once it is the only heading.
  • Project files need -std=gnu17 or later for strict builds: R’s own R_ext/Complex.h uses an anonymous struct, so -std=gnu99 -Wpedantic fails inside R, not inside zucbor.
  • roxygen2 must be 8.1.0 or newer; an older one rewrites man/ on document().
  • Prose is en-GB (Language: en-GB), with domain terms in inst/WORDLIST.

Testing

  • Conformance: RFC 8949 Appendix A both ways and Appendix F as must-reject (helper-rfc8949.R, helper-rfc8949-diag.R), QCBOR’s 122 not-well-formed vectors, the cose-wg examples and the spec examples, all in tests/testthat/fixtures/ (sources and licences in its README.md). Fixtures are regenerated only with tools/update-fixtures, never by hand. cbor/test-vectors runs outside the suite through tools/run-conformance, against rule-attributed baselines.
  • Helpers (helper-expect.R): f64() and f32() build float literals from bits, because R’s parser on macOS arm64 does not round every decimal literal correctly. neg_zero() makes -0 at run time, because the byte compiler folds the literal to +0. fault_class() checks many inputs with one expectation, since per-expectation overhead dominates run time. expect_cbor() asserts exact output bytes.
  • Heavy tests that allocate millions of objects call skip_heavy(); the gctorture job sets ZUCBOR_SKIP_HEAVY.
  • Serial on purpose: no Config/testthat/parallel, so gctorture and valgrind see the C code. The suite runs in a few seconds, and no test touches the network (tools/check-no-network).

Continuous integration

Shared r-actions workflows at @v1: R-CMD-check.yaml (quick on a pull request, full after merge or with full-ci) and coverage.yaml. native-checks.yaml calls the shared sanitizers (UBSan, and ASan containers driven by tools/sanitizer-exercise.R, both with -UNDEBUG), valgrind, LTO, gctorture (quick on a pull request, step 100 after merge), a blocking rchk, and runs tools/run-conformance; it also runs weekly. vendor.yaml calls the shared vendor check and runs tools/check-status-table.

Package-owned: hardening.yaml runs tools/run-lint, tools/run-mutation-check, tools/check-no-network and tools/run-fuzz (2 minutes per target on a pull request, 30 nightly). pkgdown.yaml deploys the site with development: mode: auto, so a .9000 version builds into dev/ beside the release.

Vendored native code

TinyCBOR (intel/tinycbor), MIT, tag v7.0, commit 6442e749, imported 2026-09-30, with no local patches. src/vendor/PROVENANCE records the tarball SHA-256 (trust on first use) and the compile configuration; tools/tinycbor-files.txt lists the byte-identical subset (parser, validator, error strings). The two headers upstream generates at CMake time live in the project-owned src/tinycbor/, written by tools/update-tinycbor. src/zu_tinycbor_check.c fails the build if ZU_MAX_DEPTH_CAP differs from CBOR_PARSER_MAX_RECURSIONS. There is deliberately no Makevars.win, so one OBJECTS list cannot drift. The build traps (C23, MinGW formats, half-float intrinsics, GCC < 11) are design §13.

Pull requests

Stacked pull requests: retarget the next one to main before deleting a merged base branch; deleting it first closes the dependent pull request.
